blogTitle: The Captain's Log (color coded, tabs on the right)
about: [RED] Welcome to the command post. I'm Ashley, captain of the Eagles varsity cheer squad (12 girls, 1 coach, 1 mascot who is a bird). Cheer is a sport. We have a season, a schedule, a legend and a binder. Competition season runs November through February and I treat it like a military campaign because it is one, with more glitter. Everything on this page is color coded. The legend is below. [YELLOW] means optional. [YELLOW] is never optional. I've never dropped anyone. I've been the base on the 3-high for two seasons, catching people since the 9th grade. Someone has to be the floor. [PINK] I like your shoes.
aboutMore: THE LEGEND: [RED] mandatory. [ORANGE] snacks (yes, oranges, it started as a joke and now it's policy). [YELLOW] optional (it isn't). [GREEN] good news, go. [BLUE] bows, ribbons, hair. [PURPLE] emergency (injury, tears, group chat). [PINK] personal, nice, off the record. Standing order #1: be early. #2: if you're early you're on time. #3: nobody falls. #14: Brittany, we are not discussing spot 5.
meet: Who I'd like to meet: whoever invented the pom-pom (I'd like to shake their hand and give them 12 notes on durability). The Regionals judge who gave us a 7.2 for showmanship last year (I have the sheet, it's in the RED folder). Coach Dunleavy, about the pep rally, which he has now moved three times. Chad, in a meeting, about the mascot suit. And whoever controls the weather on competition day. [PURPLE] We need to talk.

interests.General: cheer (varsity, 4th year, base), the squad (12), color-coded binders (one per routine), whiteboards, label makers (I own three), oranges (literal), 5:45 AM, stunting, competition spreadsheets (with tabs), bobby pins (I carry 40), the pool (offseason), being early, helping people carry things, saying 'copy' instead of 'ok'

interests.Movies: Bring It On (a documentary), Legally Blonde (a binder and a plan, that's all it takes), Remember the Titans (the captain parts are real), Miracle (the speech), Mean Girls (the pyramid in it is wrong), Bring It On Again (fine)
interests.Television: Friday Night Lights (new, I watch it for the sideline shots), Dancing with the Stars (I score along), America's Next Top Model (Tyra's rules are standing orders), the national cheer championships on tape (watched it 40 times), Laguna Beach (LC has a plan too)
interests.Books: my competition binder (4 inches), the high school spirit rules handbook (read it twice, there's a section on pom-pom size), Seventeen (I score the quizzes), How to Win Friends and Influence People (Coach Dana gave it to me, I take notes), Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants (the first one)
interests.Heroes: Coach Dana, my mom (a nurse, 12 hour night shifts, knows everyone on every floor), my cousin Tasha (taught me to base, went to college, I never thanked her properly), the flyers (they trust me with their lives daily), Jenna (see blog), anybody who's ever stood at the top of a pyramid and said 'ready?'

bulletins.subject: STANDING ORDERS (for everyone, not only the squad)
bulletins.body: 1) Be early. 2) If you're early you're on time. 3) If you're on time you're late. 4) Label your things. 5) Bring a spare hair tie. 6) Say 'copy' when you hear an instruction. 7) If a flyer waves, wave back. 8) Never drop the nachos. 9) Nobody falls. That's it. That's the whole list. I've been told it's 'a lot.' It's 9. I have 14 in the binder. [PINK] Now go have a nice day. I mean that. It's in the legend.

blog.title: 5:45 AM: a day, color coded
blog.body: [PURPLE] 5:45 AM: whiteboard in the garage. REGIONALS: 118 DAYS. Mom comes home from the hospital. We swap places in the kitchen like a relay. [GREEN] 6:30: bus. [RED] 7:15 to 2:50: school (this is the part with the least color, honestly). [ORANGE] 3:45: practice. Snack rotation: Courtney. [BLUE] 5:30: hair for tomorrow. [PINK] 6:45: dinner, and I make a chart for my little brother Noah, who's 9: GREEN, homework done. YELLOW, bath (optional) (it's not). [PURPLE] 7:00: Mom leaves for her night shift. We wave from the porch. She says 'you're doing great.' I say 'copy.' She says 'don't say copy to your mother.' I say 'copy.' [GREEN] 10:00: sleep. I set three alarms. All three are color coded. I like to know what time it is.

blog.title: The Day I Dropped Jenna (a post I've been meaning to write)
blog.body: 9th grade. A Tuesday. 4:12 PM. I'd been a base for six weeks and I was very proud of my arms. Jenna was our flyer, 90 pounds and no fear. We were running the basket toss and I looked up one half second too late. She hit the mat. She was fine. She'd landed on her side and she laughed and said 'whoops,' but I couldn't breathe and I sat on the floor of the gym for eleven minutes. That night I got a note in my locker. It was folded very small. It said: 'it's ok. catch me again.' I've kept it. I've caught her about 400 times since. Zero drops. I'm told I'm 'intense about safety.' This is why. I don't do the flips. I'm the floor. And someone has to be the floor, and she trusted me to be it. I'll never be done earning that.

blog.title: Movies about cheerleading, graded (by a cheerleader)
blog.body: BRING IT ON: A-. The spirit fingers are correct. The Regionals scene is accurate to the point of trauma. I flinched at the audition. LEGALLY BLONDE: A. She has a binder. She has a plan. She is a cheerleader and she wins by being prepared. This is the most accurate movie about my life. MEAN GIRLS: B. The pyramid in the gym is not a pyramid. It's a wobble. Nobody would let that pass inspection. BRING IT ON AGAIN: C. Not enough captain. Not enough tabs. Too much 'we're just here to have fun.' We're here to have fun and also to win. Both can be true. They can both be color coded. [PINK] But it's still a good movie. I watched it on a Saturday. I cried at the end. Nobody saw. It's in the folder.
